label: nyiso 12 interchange-shaping
definition: (PROBE — REJECTED.) Mechanism-A test on the nyiso 11 keeper config: adds --interchange-shaping, which caps each priced import tranche's availability by the MEASURED EIA-930 month x hour-of-day p90 net-import envelope (no fitted constant) to fix the static node's flat-schedule diurnal defect. It DOES fix the shape (net-import hour-of-day corr vs measured 2023 +0.69->+0.96, 2025 -0.86->+0.24), confirming the 2025 over-import/diurnal-mis-shape diagnosis is real. BUT the p90 net-import cap is tighter than the keeper's flat economic clearing in most buckets, so it starves baseload imports: net interchange falls to 60.6/74.9/71.6% of measured (2024 & 2025 go from in-band to OUT of the +/-15% interchange band), in-state gas rises (2025 -6.4%->+5.0% vs EIA-930), and the demand-weighted monthly LMP MAE WORSENS every year (8.0/4.3/6.3 -> 9.6/7.5/8.3). Per the volume-band guardrail (a shape gain bought by breaking a volume band is a zero-sum trade -> report and stop), REJECTED; keeper nyiso 11 stands. The off-the-shelf shaping is CAISO-shaped (gross-import cap to a net envelope); the right NYISO tool is a firm/baseload must-flow tranche or a level-preserving diurnal re-weight (see docs/nyiso-backcast-residual-attribution-2026-06.md).
